ex_en: Your son is stubborn, he doesn't listen.
note: f. عنيدة 3nīda; pl. عنيدين 3nīdīn. Libyans also say راسه قاسح (his head is hard).

ex_ar: الولد هذا قليل الأدب مع الناس الكبار.
ex_tr: il-weld hādha gallīl il-adab ma3 in-nās il-kbār.
ex_en: This boy is rude with older people.
note: f. قليلة الأدب gallīlt il-adab; pl. قليلين الأدب. Opposite of مربي.

ex_ar: خوك شجاع، ما يخافش من حد.
ex_en: Your brother is brave, he's afraid of nobody.
note: pl. شجعان shuj3ān. Libyan speech also uses راجل (a real man) for brave.

ex_en: Don't be a coward, go talk to him.
note: f. جبانة jbāna; pl. جبناء jubanā' / جبانين jbānīn.

phrases.en: that guy is a coward, he ran away

ex_en: Behave and I'll bring you a sweet.
note: f. عاقلة 3āgla; pl. عاقلين 3āglīn. Very common with children: كون عاقل "behave".

phrases.en: your daughter is so well-behaved, mashallah

ex_en: My brother knows a lot about electricity.
note: f. فاهمة fāhma; pl. فاهمين fāhmīn. Active participle used as adjective: انت فاهم؟ "do you get it?"

phrases.en: do you get what I mean?

ex_en: Our neighbour is a decent man.
note: f. محترمة mu7tarama; pl. محترمين mu7taramīn.

ex_en: Leave the money with him, he's trustworthy.
note: f. أمينة amīna; pl. أمناء umanā'.

phrases.en: he's not trustworthy, watch out for him

ex_en: He turned out to be a traitor and sold us out.
note: f. خاينة khāyna; pl. خونة khawana.

ex_ar: ما تكونش طماع، خذ نصيبك بس.
ex_tr: ma tkūnsh Tammā3, khudh nSībak bass.
ex_en: Don't be greedy, take only your share.
note: f. طماعة Tammā3a; pl. طماعين Tammā3īn.

phrases.en: the greedy man is never satisfied

ex_en: Don't tell her, she's envious.
note: f. حسودة 7asūda. Libyans fear the evil eye: عينه حارة "he has an envious eye".

ex_ar: من يوم صار مدير وهو متكبر.
ex_tr: min yōm Sār mudīr w huwwa mitkabbir.
ex_en: Since he became a manager he's been arrogant.
note: f. متكبرة mitkabbra; pl. متكبرين mitkabbrīn.

ex_ar: من يوم شرى الكرهبة وهو شايف روحه.
ex_tr: min yōm shra l-karhba w huwwa shāyif rū7ah.
ex_en: Since he bought the car he's been full of himself.
note: f. شايفة روحها shāyfa rū7ha; pl. شايفين رواحهم shāyfīn rwā7hum. Lit. "seeing himself".

phrases.en: you think you're better than us?

ex_en: Although he is rich, he is humble.
note: f. متواضعة mitwāD3a; pl. متواضعين mitwāD3īn.

ex_en: My mother is very patient with us.

phrases.en: the teacher is patient with the kids

ex_en: My dad is a bit irritable in the morning.
The doctor is very gentle with the kids.
note: f. لطيفة laTīfa; pl. لطاف luTāf.

ex_en: Their daughter is modest and well brought-up.
note: f. حشيمة 7ashīma. Libyan praise for a decent, modest person, from حشمة.

phrases.en: a reserved man who doesn't talk much

ex_en: Your friend is so funny, we laughed a lot.
note: f. دمها خفيف dammha khfīf; pl. دمهم خفيف dammhum khfīf.

ex_ar: ما نحبش نقعد معاه، دمه ثقيل.
ex_tr: ma n7ibbsh nug3ud m3āh, dammah thgīl.
ex_en: I don't like sitting with him, he's unbearable.
note: f. دمها ثقيل dammha thgīl; pl. دمهم ثقيل dammhum thgīl.

ex_en: Are you serious or joking?
note: f. جدية jiddiyya; pl. جديين jiddiyyīn.

phrases.en: the teacher is very serious in class

ex_ar: الصغار هذول مؤدبين ما شاء الله.
ex_tr: iS-Sghār hadhōl mu'addabīn mā shā' allāh.
ex_en: These kids are well-mannered, mashallah.
note: f. مؤدبة mu'addaba; pl. مؤدبين mu'addabīn.

ex_ar: أختي منظمة، كل حاجة في بلاصتها.
ex_en: My sister is organized, everything is in its place.
This student neglects his studies.
note: f. مهملة muhmila; pl. مهملين muhmilīn.

ex_en: Your room is messy, tidy it up a bit.
My friend is loyal, he never let me down.
note: f. مخلصة mukhliSa; pl. مخلصين mukhliSīn.

ex_en: The dog is loyal to its owner.
note: f. وفية wafiyya; pl. أوفياء awfiyā'.

ex_en: The wolf is cunning in folk tales.
note: f. مكارة makkāra; pl. مكارين makkārīn.

ex_en: His words are malicious, he means something by them.
note: f. خبيثة khabītha; pl. خبثاء khubathā'.

ex_en: The boy is innocent, he didn't do anything.
note: f. بريئة barī'a; pl. أبرياء abriyā'.

phrases.en: he was found innocent in court

ex_ar: هو على نيته، يصدق أي حد.
ex_en: He's naive, he believes anyone.
note: f. على نيتها 3la niyyt-ha; pl. على نياتهم 3la niyyāt-hum.

ex_en: He's hard-hearted, he shows no mercy.
note: f. قاسية gāsya; pl. قاسيين gāsyīn. (Different from قاسح "hard to the touch".)

ex_ar: جارتنا فضولية، تبي تعرف كل شي.
ex_tr: jāratna fuDūliyya, tibbi ta3rif kull shay.
ex_en: Our neighbour is nosy, she wants to know everything.
note: f. فضولية fuDūliyya; pl. فضوليين fuDūliyyīn.

ex_en: My aunt is so chatty, she never stops.
note: f. كثيرة الهدرة kthīrt il-hadra. From هدرز "to chat".

ex_en: My uncle is a level-headed man, people listen to him.
He drives recklessly, he's going to cause an accident.
note: f. متهورة mitahawwra; pl. متهورين mitahawwrīn.

ex_ar: ولدي واعي، يعرف يقطع الشارع وحده.
ex_tr: weldi wā3i, ya3rif yigTa3 ish-shāri3 wa7dah.
ex_en: My son is careful, he can cross the street alone.
note: f. واعية wā3ya; pl. واعيين wā3yīn.

ex_ar: البايع هذا غشاش، ما تشريش منه.
ex_tr: il-bāyi3 hādha ghashshāsh, ma tishrīsh minnah.
ex_en: This seller is a cheat, don't buy from him.
note: f. غشاشة ghashshāsha; pl. غشاشين ghashshāshīn.

phrases.en: a student who cheats on exams

ex_tr: guddāmak yiD7ak w warāk yitkallam, munāfig.
ex_en: He smiles to your face and talks behind your back, a hypocrite.
note: f. منافقة munāfga; pl. منافقين munāfgīn.

ex_en: Their family is religious, they pray at the mosque.
note: f. متدينة mitdayyna; pl. متدينين mitdayynīn.

ex_en: An ambitious girl, she wants to become a doctor.
note: f. طموحة Tamū7a. Also a noun "ambition".

ex_en: Your son is diligent in his studies.
note: f. مجتهدة mujtahda; pl. مجتهدين mujtahdīn.

phrases.en: every hard worker gets his share (proverb)

ex_en: My sister is sociable, she loves people.
note: f. اجتماعية ijtimā3iyya. Also "social" as in social media (مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي).

phrases.en: he's not sociable, he likes to be alone

ex_en: Don't make fun of him, he's sensitive.
note: f. حساسة 7assāsa; pl. حساسين 7assāsīn. Also حساسية "allergy".

ex_ar: هي عاطفية هلبة، تبكي على أي حاجة.
ex_en: She's very emotional, she cries over anything.

en: keen on; fond of; passionate about
ex_ar: خوي غاوي كورة، ما يفوتش ماتش.
ex_tr: khūy ghāwi kūra, ma yfawwitsh mātsh.
ex_en: My brother is crazy about football, he never misses a match.
note: f. غاوية ghāwya; pl. غاويين ghāwyīn. Followed directly by the thing: غاوي كورة.

ex_ar: الصغير مدلع، كل شي يبيه يجيبوهوله.
ex_tr: iS-Sghīr mdalla3, kull shay yibbih yjībūhūlah.
ex_en: The little one is spoiled, they get him everything he wants.
note: f. مدلعة mdall3a; pl. مدلعين mdall3īn.

ex_en: I'm optimistic, things will get better.
Why are you always pessimistic?
I'm sure he'll come.
note: f. واثقة wāthga; pl. واثقين wāthgīn. واثق من روحه "self-confident".

ex_ar: راجل شهم، وقف معانا في الأزمة.
ex_tr: rājil shahm, wgif m3āna fi l-azma.
ex_en: A gallant man, he stood by us in the crisis.
note: pl. شهام shhām. High praise for a man who helps others.

ex_en: He left her on the street, a scoundrel.

ex_tr: min yōm nja7 w huwwa maghrūr.
ex_en: Since he passed he's been conceited.

phrases.en: a girl vain about her looks

ex_en: A trivial problem, it's not worth it.
note: f. تافهة tāfha; pl. تافهين tāfhīn.

ex_en: My grandfather is a wise man.
note: f. حكيمة 7akīma; pl. حكماء 7ukamā'. In some areas حكيم also means "doctor".

ex_en: Are you crazy? Driving at this speed!
note: f. مجنونة majnūna; pl. مجانين majānīn. Libyans also say مهبول (milder).

ex_en: You're responsible for your younger siblings.
note: f. مسؤولة mas'ūla; pl. مسؤولين mas'ūlīn. Also a noun "official".

ex_tr: iS-Sghīr gāfiz, yifhamha w hiyya Tāyra.
ex_en: The little one is sharp, he gets it immediately.
note: f. قافزة gāfza; pl. قافزين gāfzīn. Typically Libyan; also used ironically for a smart-alec.

phrases.en: a girl who's sharp at maths

ex_en: He's good at business.
note: f. فالحة fāl7a. Often sarcastic: فالح غير في الأكل "good only at eating".

phrases.en: a girl who's capable at everything

ex_en: He spoke to him politely.

ex_ar: الصغير بكاي، يبكي على أي حاجة.
ex_en: The little one is a crybaby, he cries over anything.

phrases.en: a girl who cries a lot

ex_en: He's always grumpy, he never laughs.

phrases.en: don't be a killjoy at the wedding

ex_en: Come in, don't be shy.
note: f. مستحية mista7ya; pl. مستحيين mista7yīn.

phrases.en: the little girl is shy with the guests
I'm too shy to tell him

ex_en: A bold question, but fine.
My dad is careful with money.
His wife is a spendthrift, she spends everything.
My mum is forgiving, she forgets quickly.

ex_ar: ما تكونش أناني، قسم مع خوك.
ex_tr: ma tkūnsh anāni, gassim ma3 khūk.
ex_en: Don't be selfish, share with your brother.
Don't hold a grudge, forgive him.
This noise is very annoying.
A cheerful girl, always smiling.
Why are you frowning today?

phrases.en: he always has a sour face

ex_en: He's not dull, he just doesn't study.
My uncle is cultured, he reads lots of books.
His mother is educated and works.
My grandmother is illiterate, she can't read.
note: f. أمية ummiyya; pl. أميين. Do not confuse with أمي "my mother".

ex_en: In the film this man is the villain.
Smoking is harmful to health.
Our neighbour is helpful, he helps everyone.
The employee was arrogant with us.
People here are friendly.
To be frank with you, I didn't like it.
note: f. صريحة Sarī7a. نكون صريح معاك "to be honest with you".

ex_en: Quiet, the baby is asleep.
note: f. نايمة nāyma; pl. نايمين nāymīn. Libyans also say راقد.

ex_en: My dad is asleep, don't shout.
note: f. راقدة rāgda; pl. راقدين rāgdīn. Libyan رقد "to sleep".

phrases.en: I found him asleep on the sofa

ex_en: Have you been awake since early?
note: f. فايقة fāyga; pl. فايقين fāygīn. Libyan فاق "to wake up".

ex_en: He was driving drunk.
note: f. سكرانة sakrāna; pl. سكارى sakāra.

ex_en: He's sick, he's not fasting today.
note: f. فاطرة fāTra; pl. فاطرين fāTrīn.

ex_en: His wife is seven months pregnant.
note: pl. حوامل 7awāmil. Only feminine in sense (مرته حامل).

ex_ar: خوي الكبير معرس وعنده زوز صغار.
ex_tr: khūy il-kbīr m3arris w 3andah zūz Sghār.
ex_en: My older brother is married with two kids.
note: f. معرسة m3arrsa; pl. معرسين m3arrsīn. Libyan, from عرّس "to marry". Also متزوج mitzawwij.

ex_en: She's been married for five years.
note: f. متزوجة mitzawwja; pl. متزوجين mitzawwjīn.

ex_en: He's still single, he hasn't married.
She's divorced and has a daughter.
note: f. مطلقة mTallga; pl. مطلقين mTallgīn.

ex_en: My grandfather has been a widower for a long time.
note: f. أرملة armla; pl. أرامل arāmil.

ex_en: My sister is engaged, the wedding is in summer.
note: f. مخطوبة makhTūba. Usually said of the woman.

en: unemployed; out of work; broken down
ex_en: My cousin has been unemployed for a year.

phrases.en: the machine is out of order

ex_en: The teacher is absent today.
note: f. غايبة ghāyba; pl. غايبين ghāybīn.

phrases.en: away from home for a week

ex_en: All the students are present.
note: f. حاضرة 7āDra; pl. حاضرين 7āDrīn. As a reply to a request: حاضر "right away".

ex_en: Is Mohammed in? — No, he went out.
note: f. موجودة mawjūda; pl. موجودين mawjūdīn. Very common: موجود؟ "is he in?"

phrases.en: bread is available at the bakery

ex_en: I'm willing to help you.
note: f. مستعدة mista3idda; pl. مستعدين mista3iddīn.

ex_en: The key is lost, I can't find it.
note: f. ضايعة Dāy3a; pl. ضايعين Dāy3īn.

ex_en: We were lost on the road for an hour.
note: f. تايهة tāyha; pl. تايهين tāyhīn.

phrases.en: lost, doesn't know where he's going

ex_en: There are two injured in the accident.
note: f. مصابة muSāba; pl. مصابين muSābīn.

ex_en: Our neighbours' son has been locked up for a month.
note: f. محبوسة ma7būsa; pl. محبوسين ma7būsīn.

phrases.en: the cat is shut in the room

ex_en: A spot for disabled people.
note: f. معاقة mu3āga; pl. معاقين mu3āgīn. Polite: من ذوي الإعاقة.

ex_en: Is the AC on?
note: f. شغالة shaghghāla. Libyan: الكهربا شغالة "the power is on".

ex_en: The light is off, I can't see.
note: f. طافية Tāfya. Libyan: الضي طافي "the light is off".

phrases.en: the power has been off since the morning

ex_en: I left the light on in the room.
note: f. شاعلة shā3la. Libyan: الضي شاعل "the light is on".

ex_en: I can't stay, I'm in a hurry.
note: f. مزروبة mazrūba; pl. مزروبين mazrūbīn. Very Libyan, from زرب "to hurry".

phrases.en: why are you in such a rush?

ex_en: The matter is closed, that's it.
The bill is settled, you owe nothing.
note: f. خالصة khālSa. Also used as an adverb "at all" (مش باهي خالص).

phrases.en: the rent is paid for this month

ex_en: Entry is free for children.
note: f. مجانية majjāniyya. Libyans also say بلاش.

ex_en: She's taken, she has a fiancé.

ex_tr: būy aSla3 min w huwwa Sghīr.
ex_en: My dad has been bald since he was young.
note: f. صلعة Sal3a; pl. صلع Sul3. Libyans also say راسه أملس.

phrases.en: a bald man with a beard

ex_en: Her hair is curly and long.

phrases.en: the shirt is creased, iron it

ex_en: His hair is soft as silk.
He became skinny after the illness.
note: f. نحيفة n7īfa; pl. نحاف n7āf.

phrases.en: you need to eat, you're skinny

ex_en: This man is huge, as big as a door.
note: f. ضخمة Dakhma; pl. ضخام Dkhām.

ex_en: Her groom is handsome and decent.
note: pl. وسيمين wasīmīn. Libyans more often say زين or مزيان for looks.

ex_ar: جدي ولى أعمى في آخر عمره.
ex_en: My grandfather went blind late in life.

phrases.en: are you blind? didn't you see it?

ex_en: Speak loudly, my grandad is a bit deaf.
note: f. طرشا Tarsha; pl. طرش Tursh.

ex_en: Our neighbours' son is mute, he speaks with signs.
note: f. خرسا kharsa; pl. خرس khurs.

phrases.en: he went silent like a mute
don't just sit there silent, speak

ex_en: He's been limping since the accident.
The little one is a bit cross-eyed, he needs glasses.

phrases.en: he's not cross-eyed, he's winking at you

ex_en: The pirate is one-eyed in the film.

phrases.en: in the land of the blind the one-eyed man is king

ex_en: My son is left-handed, he writes with his left.

ex_ar: أختي متحجبة من وهي في الإعدادي.
ex_tr: ukhti mit7ajjba min w hiyya fi l-i3dādi.
ex_en: My sister has worn the hijab since middle school.
note: Feminine only; pl. متحجبات mit7ajjbāt. Also محجبة m7ajjba.

ex_en: You're dressed smart today, where are you off to?
note: Invariable (French chic). Very common in Libya.

ex_en: Her father is always an elegant man.
The room is tidy and clean.
note: f. مرتبة mrattba. Note: as a noun مرتّب also means "salary".

ex_en: The kitchen is cluttered, there are lots of dishes.
note: f. مكركبة mkarkba. Common Libyan for a cluttered place.

ex_ar: يمشي للجيم كل يوم، ولى معضل.
ex_tr: yimshi l-il-jīm kull yōm, walla m3aDDal.
ex_en: He goes to the gym every day, he's got buff.
note: f. معضلة m3aDDla. Libyan/Arabic slang from عضلة.

ex_en: My uncle is pot-bellied from eating.

phrases.en: he got a belly after the wedding

ex_en: He came back from the beach tanned.

phrases.en: his face is tanned from the sun

ex_en: Your face is pale, are you sick?

phrases.en: the shirt has faded from washing

ex_en: His face is pale with fear.
That bearded man is our neighbour.
note: pl. ملتحيين milti7yīn. Also بلحية b-li7ya "with a beard".

ex_en: The car is fixed, you can take it.
note: f. مصلحة mSall7a. From صلّح "to fix".

phrases.en: the phone is repaired and works

en: broken down; out of order; delayed
ex_en: The lift is out of order, take the stairs.

phrases.en: the car broke down on the road

ex_en: The kids left the toy broken.
note: f. مخربة mkharrba. From خرّب "to break/ruin".

phrases.en: the road is ruined, all potholes
the house is damaged from the war

ex_en: This meat is spoiled, throw it away.
note: f. فاسدة fāsda; pl. فاسدين fāsdīn.

ex_en: The bread is mouldy, it has green on it.
This fish is rotten, it smells bad.
note: f. خامجة khāmja. Libyan word for bad-smelling, gone-off things; also an insult.

ex_en: This watch is fake, not original.
note: f. مزيفة mzayyfa. Libyans also say تقليد for knock-off goods.

ex_en: These trainers are knock-offs, they're cheap.
note: Used like an adjective after a noun: شنطة تقليد "a knock-off bag".

ex_en: The market is crowded today, Thursday.
This sofa is very comfortable.
Travelling by car is tiring.
This book is very useful.
Too much sugar is harmful.
This film is boring, I fell asleep.
note: f. مملة mumilla. Libyans also say يقلّق "it's boring".

ex_en: The trip was very enjoyable.
The view is wonderful from up there.
note: f. رائعة rā'i3a. More formal than هايل.

ex_en: The traffic today is terrible.
note: f. فظيعة faDHī3a. Like English "awesome/awful", context decides.

phrases.en: the food is amazing, bless your hands

ex_en: The road is scary at night.

ex_ar: الحي هذا آمن، ما فيهش مشاكل.
ex_tr: il-7ayy hādha āmin, ma fīhsh mashākil.
ex_en: This neighbourhood is safe, there's no trouble.

phrases.en: the road isn't safe at night

ex_en: This job is a sure thing, don't worry.
It's impossible to get there in an hour.
note: Also used alone as an exclamation: مستحيل! "no way!".

phrases.en: no way! I don't believe it

ex_en: You must come tomorrow.
note: f. ضرورية Darūriyya. ضروري تجي "you must come".

ex_en: Is the food enough for everyone?
note: f. كافية kāfya. Libyans often say يكفي or بزايد.

ex_en: Is there an extra chair?
note: f. زايدة zāyda. Also "plus" in arithmetic.

phrases.en: there's a bit too much salt

ex_en: He has a private driver.
note: f. خاصة khāSSa. Also خاص بـ "specific to".

ex_en: The public hospital is crowded.
The official holiday is on Thursday.
This is a personal question.
note: f. شخصية shakhSiyya. Also "in person": شخصيا.

ex_en: These tomatoes are local, not imported.
A hundred percent natural honey.
This grass is artificial, not natural.
This shop is well known in Tripoli.
note: f. معروفة ma3rūfa. Also as noun "a favour".

ex_en: This number is unknown, I don't recognise it.
My siblings are very different from each other.
Your son looks a lot like you.
note: f. شبيهة shbīha. Libyans often say يشبه or زي.

ex_en: Now isn't a good time.

phrases.en: an outfit suitable for the wedding

ex_en: The passport is valid until next year.

phrases.en: the water isn't fit to drink

ex_en: This isn't legal.
Most things in the market are imported.
Is the clock right?
note: f. مظبوطة maDbūTa. Also "exactly!" as a reply.

ex_en: You must be precise in the accounts.

ex_ar: راجل غامض، ما يحكيش على روحه.
ex_en: A mysterious man, he doesn't talk about himself.

phrases.en: the matter is a bit unclear

ex_en: Is the lesson clear?
The paperwork at the municipality is complicated.
A small problem, it'll be solved.
note: f. بسيطة basīTa; pl. بسطاء busaTā'. بسيطة! "no big deal!"

ex_en: This hotel is luxurious, very expensive.
We love Libyan home-style food.
She wore the traditional outfit at the wedding.
A modern building downtown.
My aunt wears modern clothes.
This stamp is very rare.
This illness is widespread in winter.
You're wearing the shirt inside out!

phrases.en: an overturned car on the road

ex_en: The picture is crooked, straighten it.
Go straight and then turn right.
note: Invariable in Libyan speech. Also امشي عدل "go straight".

ex_en: The pole is leaning a bit.
The ground here is level.
note: f. مستوية mistwya. In Libyan the "cooked" sense is very common (اللحم مستوي؟).

phrases.en: is the meat cooked or not?

ex_en: An oval mirror in the bathroom.
Careful, the knife is sharp.

ex_ar: السكينة هذي ماضية، اقطع بيها اللحم.
ex_tr: is-sikkīna hādhi māDya, igTa3 bīha l-la7am.
ex_en: This knife is sharp, cut the meat with it.
note: f. ماضية māDya. Libyan for a sharp knife; opposite مش ماضي "blunt".

ex_en: His hands are rough from work.

ex_ar: الجو رطب في طرابلس في الصيف.
ex_tr: il-jaw raTb fi Trābulus fi S-Sēf.
ex_en: The weather is humid in Tripoli in summer.
note: f. رطبة raTba. The humidity: الرطوبة.

ex_en: Drink lukewarm water in the morning.

phrases.en: the tea is lukewarm, heat it up

ex_en: The chicken is frozen, let it thaw.

ex_ar: نبي مشروب مثلج في السخانة هذي.
ex_tr: nibbi mashrūb mthallij fi s-skhāna hādhi.
ex_en: I want an ice-cold drink in this heat.
Bazin is a rich, heavy dish.
The couscous is delicious, bless your hands.
note: f. لذيذة ldhīdha. Libyans also say بنين for tasty.

ex_en: My brother is two years older than me.
note: Elative of كبير. Invariable in Libyan speech (no feminine كبرى except in set phrases). Superlative: أكبر واحد "the biggest one".

ex_en: My sister is younger than me.
The coffee here is better than over there.
note: Elative of باهي/حسن. Very common: أحسن حاجة "the best thing"; أحسن! "good, serves him right!".

phrases.en: best thing is we sleep early

ex_en: This road is worse than the first.

phrases.en: the worst day of my life

ex_en: Your son has become taller than you.

phrases.en: the tallest man on the team

ex_en: Take the shorter road.
Gold has become more expensive than before.
note: Elative of غالي. Also "dearest": أغلى ناس "dearest people".

ex_en: The popular market is cheaper than the mall.
By plane is faster than by road.
This bag is heavier than the other.

phrases.en: the heaviest thing in the house
he's even more annoying than his dad

ex_en: Take the lighter bag.
note: Elative of خفيف. أخف الضررين "the lesser evil".

ex_ar: الامتحان هذا أسهل من اللي فات.
ex_tr: il-imti7ān hādha as-hal min illi fāt.
ex_en: This exam is easier than the last one.
Maths is my hardest subject.
Where's the nearest pharmacy?
The new house is farther from work.
The world is nicer in spring.
This colour suits you better.

phrases.en: the most beautiful country in the world

ex_en: This coffee is stronger than usual.

phrases.en: the strongest team in the league

ex_en: The signal is weaker here.

phrases.en: he got weaker after the illness

ex_ar: الجامع هذا أقدم جامع في المدينة.
ex_tr: ij-jāmi3 hādha agdam jāmi3 fi l-mdīna.
ex_en: This mosque is the oldest in the old city.
Do you have a newer model?
note: Elative of جديد. Also آخر موديل "latest model".

phrases.en: the newest thing on the market

ex_en: The sea is cleaner here.

phrases.en: the cleanest restaurant in the area

ex_en: Today is hotter than yesterday.

phrases.en: the hottest month of the year

ex_en: Tonight is colder than last night.

phrases.en: the coolest spot in the house
the mountains are colder than the coast

ex_en: Health is more important than money.
note: Elative of مهم. المهم "the main thing".

phrases.en: nothing is more important than family

ex_en: It's better that you go early.
note: Slightly more formal synonym of أحسن.

ex_en: This is the worst decision I've made.
My sister is the smartest in the class.
He's the richest man in the area.

phrases.en: the richest people in the country

ex_ar: العيلة هذي أفقر عيلة في الحي.
ex_en: This family is the poorest in the neighbourhood.
The tallest building in Tripoli.
Turn the volume down, make it lower.
This room is roomier than the first.
This alley is narrower.
He's the best at maths.

phrases.en: the best cook in the family

ex_en: My mum is the kindest person in the world.
Tripoli is more beautiful at night.

phrases.en: the most beautiful day of my life

en: more dangerous; most dangerous; more serious
ex_en: The coastal road is more dangerous at night.

phrases.en: the matter is more serious than that

ex_en: The internet is slower than usual today.
The most famous Libyan dish is bazin.
Home food is healthier.
note: Elative of صحيح. الأصح "the correct way".

phrases.en: it's more correct to say it this way

ex_en: The kids are having fun at the beach.
note: f. مستانسة mistānsa; pl. مستانسين mistānsīn. Very common Libyan; from استانس "to enjoy oneself".

phrases.en: are you having a good time here?

ex_ar: من يوم فقد خدمته وهو مكتئب.
ex_tr: min yōm fgad khidmtah w huwwa mukta'ib.
ex_en: Since he lost his job he's been depressed.

ex_ar: حاسس روحي مخنوق في الحوش، نبي نطلع.
ex_tr: 7āsis rū7i makhnūg fi l-7ōsh, nibbi nuTla3.
ex_en: I feel stifled at home, I want to go out.
note: f. مخنوقة makhnūga. Libyan: حاسس روحي مخنوق "I feel suffocated (emotionally)".

ex_en: I regret what I did.
He was too embarrassed to ask.
note: f. مكسوفة maksūfa. Libyans also say محشوم.

phrases.en: her face went red, she's embarrassed

ex_en: We're all shocked by the news.
The little one is terrified of the dog.
Now I'm reassured, you arrived safely.
note: f. مطمنة mTammna. Libyan form of مطمئن.

phrases.en: I don't feel good about this man

ex_en: I'm not interested in politics.

phrases.en: he takes care of his health

ex_en: I feel frustrated with work.
I'm looking forward to seeing you.
I'm hesitant whether to go or not.
I was embarrassed in front of people.

phrases.en: don't put me in an awkward spot

ex_en: Her heart is hurt by his words.
We're all affected by this news.

phrases.en: deeply affected by his grandfather's death

ex_en: Why are you irritated? What happened?
note: f. متنرفزة mitnarfza. From French nerf; very common in Libya.

ex_en: He lives carefree, without worries.
note: f. متهنية mithannya. Libyan: نوم متهني "sound sleep".

en: in a great mood; buzzing; enjoying
ex_en: With my morning coffee I'm in a great mood.
note: f. مكيفة mkayyfa. Libyan slang from كيف "pleasure". (Homograph of مكيّف "air conditioner".)

phrases.en: you look in a great mood today

ex_en: Don't talk to her now, she's upset.
note: f. مشوشة mshawwsha. Libyan: مشوش = upset/bothered.

ex_ar: ما تكونش يائس، كل شي يتحل.
ex_tr: ma tkūnsh yā'is, kull shay yit7all.
ex_en: Don't despair, everything gets solved.

ex_ar: عيد سعيد وكل عام وانتم بخير.
ex_tr: 3īd sa3īd w kull 3ām w intum b-khēr.
ex_en: Happy Eid, and many happy returns.
note: f. سعيدة sa3īda. Common in wishes: عيد سعيد "happy Eid", يوم سعيد.

ex_en: I'm impressed by the way you work.
note: f. معجبة mu3jaba; pl. معجبين. معجب بيها "he fancies her".

ex_en: He was amazed by the view.
My grandma is in pain from her knee.
People are sympathetic to the family.
My dad is angry with me.
note: f. غضبانة ghaDbāna. More formal than متغشش; also used of God or parents' displeasure.

ex_ar: لما نجح كان طاير من الفرحة.
ex_tr: lamma nja7 kān Tāyir min il-far7a.
ex_en: When he passed he was over the moon.
note: f. طايرة من الفرحة Tāyra min il-far7a.

ex_en: I'm upset over the missed opportunity.
note: f. متقهرة mitgahhra. Libyan, related to مقهور.

ex_en: He was flustered in the interview.
I'm not convinced by what you say.
Are you sure the shop is open?
note: f. متأكدة mit'akkda; pl. متأكدين mit'akkdīn. Very common: متأكد؟ "are you sure?".

ex_en: Do you need anything from the market?
note: f. محتاجة mi7tāja; pl. محتاجين mi7tājīn. محتاج حاجة؟ "do you need anything?".

ex_ar: مش قادر نمشي، رجلي توجع فيا.
ex_tr: mush gādir nimshi, rijli twajja3 fiyya.
ex_en: I can't walk, my leg hurts.
note: f. قادرة gādra; pl. قادرين gādrīn. Libyans more often use نقدر "I can" but قادر is common too.

ex_en: Her father agrees to the marriage.
note: f. موافقة mwāfga; pl. موافقين mwāfgīn. As a reply: موافق "agreed".

ex_en: I'm used to waking up early.
note: f. متعودة mit3awda; pl. متعودين mit3awdīn. متعود على "used to".

ex_en: Why are you standing? Sit down.
note: f. واقفة wāgfa; pl. واقفين wāgfīn.

phrases.en: the car is parked in front of the house
work has come to a halt

ex_en: I have to go now.
note: f. مضطرة muDTarra. مش مضطر "you don't have to".

phrases.en: we were forced to sell the car

ex_en: I'm forced to work on Friday.
I'm waiting for you in front of the door.
note: f. مستنية mistannya; pl. مستنيين. From استنى "to wait".

phrases.en: I sat waiting for an hour

en: staying up late; awake at night
ex_en: We stayed up until dawn.

en: on the way home; heading home
ex_en: I'm heading home, do you want anything?
note: f. مروحة mraww7a; pl. مروحين mraww7īn. From روّح "to go home".

phrases.en: I found him on his way home

ex_en: The little one runs around the house naked.

phrases.ar: حاسس روحي عريان من غير تلفون
phrases.en: I feel naked without my phone

ex_en: Don't walk barefoot, the floor is cold.
He's in debt to the bank.
At the end of the month I'm always broke.
note: f. مزلطة mzallTa; pl. مزلطين. Very common Libyan/Maghrebi slang, from زلط "poverty".

phrases.en: broke, I don't have even a dinar

ex_en: The company went bankrupt.
Exhausted from the trip.
note: f. مرهقة murhaga. Libyans more often say تعبان or مهدود.

ex_en: I feel dizzy, I want to sit down.
You look out of it, did you sleep well?
note: f. مسطولة masTūla. Often used jokingly for someone not paying attention.

phrases.en: sitting zoned out in front of the TV

ex_en: You're lucky, you won the prize.

ex_ar: اليوم هذا منحوس، كل شي خسر.
ex_tr: il-yōm hādha man7ūs, kull shay khsar.
ex_en: Today is jinxed, everything broke.
The house is decorated for the wedding.
note: f. مزوقة mzawwga. Libyan زوّق "to decorate/adorn".

phrases.en: the bride is all made up

ex_en: The power has been cut since the morning.
note: f. مقطوعة magTū3a. Libyan: الكهربا مقطوعة "the power is out".

ex_en: The kitchen drain is blocked.
Your shoelace is undone.
The dog is tied up outside.
The door is locked with the key.
note: f. مقفولة magfūla. Libyans also say مسكر.

phrases.en: the shop is closed on Friday

ex_en: The phone screen is cracked.

phrases.en: my lips are chapped from the cold

ex_en: The tyre is flat, we have to change it.
note: f. مبنشرة mbanshra. Libyan, from بنشر "puncture"; a tyre repair shop is بنشري.

phrases.en: I found the car with a flat

ex_en: The sea is polluted here, don't swim.
The car is dusty from the ghibli wind.
note: f. مغبرة mghabbra. Common with the ghibli dust wind.

ex_en: The shirt is ironed and ready.
The dishes are washed.

phrases.en: the car has just been washed

ex_en: The clothes are folded in the wardrobe.
The trousers are torn at the knee.
Careful, the door is freshly painted.
This plate is decorated with gold.
The price is fixed, it doesn't go down.
The escalator at the mall.
Don't leave the food uncovered.

phrases.en: his head is uncovered in the sun

ex_en: The food is covered on the table.
The money is hidden under the mattress.
The card's PIN number.

ex_ar: فيه حوش مهجور في آخر الزنقة.
ex_en: There's an abandoned house at the end of the alley.
My grandfather has an antique watch.
note: f. عتيقة 3tīga. Often with an affectionate/nostalgic sense; المدينة العتيقة "the old town".

ex_en: The car is shiny after the wash.
The stairs are dark, turn on the light.
note: f. مظلمة muDHlima. Libyans also say فيه ظلام.

ex_en: The street is lit up in Ramadan.
note: f. مضوية mDawwya. Libyan from ضي "light".

en: reversed; backwards; the other way round
ex_en: I wrote the number backwards.
The sky is clear today.
note: f. صافية Sāfya. Also net salary: المرتب الصافي.

ex_en: The water is murky after the rain.
note: f. عكرة 3akra. مزاجه عكر "he's in a foul mood".

phrases.en: he's in a foul mood today

ex_en: The flat is vacant, do you want to see it?
note: f. خالية khālya. (Homograph of خالي "my maternal uncle".)

phrases.en: the street is empty at night

ex_en: Careful, this mushroom is poisonous.
The chips are crispy and hot.
This iron is solid.
The egg is runny, it's not cooked.
note: f. سايلة sāyla. Also noun "a liquid".

ex_en: The pencil has a sharp point.
A fine thread.
This ball is hollow inside.
These biscuits are crumbly, they fall apart.
This table is sturdy, real wood.
A transparent bag.
His body is flexible.
People love salted fish at Eid.
The rubbish stinks, take it outside.
note: f. منتنة mnattna. Libyan from نتن "stench".

ex_en: I'm Libyan, from Tripoli.
note: f. ليبية lībiyya; pl. ليبيين lībiyyīn.

ex_en: Do you speak Arabic?
note: f. عربية 3arabiyya; pl. عرب 3arab. بالعربي "in Arabic / plainly".
